segments.title: 第132章 李珞你好短
segments.content:
Rekindling the Verdant Era, Chapter 132: Li Luo, You're So Short

"Whenever I raise my head for you"

"Even my tears feel free"

"Some love is like the falling sunlight"

"Possessing and losing it at the same time"

In the living room, a song came to an end.

Ying Chanxi was immersed in the emotions of the song, clutching the lyrics Li Luo had just written down, reading along as she listened.

"The lyrics are so beautiful," Ying Chanxi couldn't help but exclaim. "I really don't know how you wrote them."

Fireworks light up bubbles, eyes chase the river of stars, a shadow sleepwalks while chasing the light, and freedom is used to describe tears.

Each image was ordinary and common, but when paired together, they created a wonderful flutter, unexpected yet inexplicably fitting.

It was like a quill pen, gently tickling one's heartstrings.

It was also like leaning against a window listening to the rain, my mind feeling as if it had eaten a bag of Pop Rocks, that crackling, marvelous sensation.

Ying Chanxi's Chinese literature grades were not bad, but she thought for a moment and realized she probably couldn't write sentences like these.

Perhaps on a lucky day, when inspiration struck, she might come up with something occasionally. But there was no way she could, as if they were free, incorporate so many evocative descriptions into a single song.

Originally, Ying Chanxi had thought that the simple lyrical style of "Waiting For You After School" was Li Luo's songwriting style.

But unexpectedly, with the appearance of "The Light Chaser," the lyrics of "Waiting For You After School" suddenly paled in comparison.

It wasn't to say one was better than the other, but the poetic, beautiful words of "The Light Chaser" were clearly more able to touch the literary soul in certain people.

The lyrical content of "Waiting For You After School," on the other hand, was relatively straightforward, its emotional expression not as subtle as "The Light Chaser."

The former was like a brave boy's confession, while the latter was like an emotionally delicate girl.

Each had its own flavor.

However.

"I feel like the music video for this song will be hard to shoot," Ying Chanxi said, a little troubled. "Fireworks, ocean waves, fireflies, and rainbows."

"That's why we need Director Ying to take charge."

"Hmph." Ying Chanxi was inwardly pleased, but on the surface, she said impassively, "Let's finish filming 'Waiting For You After School' first."

"It's all up to you."

After sharing the song, Li Luo went to make lunch.

After lunch and a short rest, the three of them went to school together.

Xu Youyu had to continue handling some sports meet matters, while Ying Chanxi had to continue her training for the math competition.

Li Luo carried his schoolbag and a plastic bag. After parting ways with Ying Chanxi at the third-floor landing, he walked into the Class Eight classroom.

At this time, there were already about a dozen students in the classroom.

Their mid-term exam results had been less than ideal, so they chose to come to school for supplementary lessons on Sunday afternoon.

After a little preparation in the classroom, they went one by one with paper and pen to their assigned classrooms for the lessons their teachers had arranged in advance.

As for Li Luo, he waited at his seat for a short while before Yan Zhusheng arrived.

"Thank you for the computer yesterday. It was very useful."

"You're welcome." Yan Zhusheng blinked and put her schoolbag on her seat. "Are we going to the activity room now?"

"Yeah, but wait a moment." Li Luo rummaged through his plastic bag and then handed something to Yan Zhusheng.

Yan Zhusheng took it curiously and found that it was an extremely small harmonica.

"A gift for you," Li Luo said. "When I went to your house to record the song, I saw the instruments in your recording studio. I figured you probably weren't lacking any of those, so I could only give you a little trinket."

"It's okay." Yan Zhusheng's eyes sparkled. After carefully unwrapping the plastic packaging, she took out the harmonica.

She brought the harmonica to her lips, briefly tested the notes, and then began to play softly. The melody of "The Light Chaser" instantly filled the classroom.

"You learn very quickly," Li Luo said with some surprise. "I just wrote the sheet music yesterday, and you've already perfected it today?"

"I practiced at home last night," Yan Zhusheng said. "Do you want to find some time to come to my house and record the song?"

Li Luo shook his head and said with a wry smile, "You should sing this one. I think it might be because I sang 'Waiting For You After School' that your mom's company wasn't interested."

"That's not it," Yan Zhusheng said, shaking her head. "They mainly focus on film, television, and variety shows. Other than my mom, the company doesn't have many singers."

"Besides, physical albums don't sell well anymore, so being a singer isn't as profitable as it used to be."

"Many professional singers are transitioning, no longer focusing solely on album production."

"Unless it's a song that's stunning at first listen, or one written by a well-known composer, it's very difficult for them to pick it up."

Hearing Yan Zhusheng's explanation, Li Luo could understand.

"So how is 'Annual Rings' doing now?"

"'Annual Rings' is already being re-recorded," Yan Zhusheng said. "Auntie Luo Fei made a new arrangement, and my mom is singing it."

"As for the TV drama, it will probably air at the end of the month."

"We'll be able to watch it online then."

Li Luo didn't have high hopes for "Annual Rings." After all, when it was posted online before, it hadn't made much of a splash.

Most of the listeners were readers of "I'm Really Not a Star."

And as for the drama "Immortal Fate of the Jasper Pool," Li Luo hadn't watched that kind of thing much in his past life, so he knew nothing about it.

But since he hadn't heard of it, it probably wasn't very popular back then.

So Li Luo lowered his expectations.

In any case, the TV-related broadcasting rights for the song were sold and the money was in his pocket. Whether it did well or not in the future was no longer his concern.

After chatting about these things, the two of them tidied up a bit and headed to the activity room together.

The harmonica Li Luo bought came with a small carrying pouch. After putting the harmonica away, Yan Zhusheng could slip it right into her pocket, so she carried it with her.

As they were going downstairs, they happened to run into Xie Shuchen and Liu Shaowen.

"Hey, Li Luo." Liu Shaowen greeted him warmly upon seeing him. "Are you two going to practice with Xie Shuchen?"

Li Luo nodded and politely asked back, "Where are you headed?"

"To the physics competition training," Liu Shaowen said. "The classroom is on the second-year side, so I have to hurry downstairs."

"By the way," Xie Shuchen, who was beside them, looked at Li Luo and then said with a teasing smile, "Li Luo, did you sign up for the 3000-meter race?"

"Yeah, what's up?"

"This kid, Liu Shaowen, signed up too," Xie Shuchen chuckled. "You two can cheer each other on."

"You think I wanted to sign up?" Liu Shaowen said irritably. "I'll be lucky if I can even finish the race."

"Then who told you to be an idiot and sign up for the 3000-meter?" Xie Shuchen said with a pout. "The moment you saw Ying Chanxi volunteer for the 1500-meter, you went brain-dead and signed up for the 3000-meter without a second thought. You really moved yourself, didn't you?"

"What do you know?" Liu Shaowen's brows shot up. "Ying Chanxi even praised me. She said I was contributing to the class, unlike someone who was so eager to grab the 100-meter and 200-meter. If you don't place, we'll see how I laugh at you."

Watching the two of them bickering playfully, Yan Zhusheng couldn't help but whisper to Li Luo, "Xixi is so popular."

"You have the nerve to say that?" Li Luo chuckled. "There are plenty of guys who like you too, you know."

"What about you?" Yan Zhusheng tilted her head to look at him, throwing a direct question with an innocent expression. "Do you like me too?"

"Let's talk about it when you get rid of those dark circles under your eyes," Li Luo said, pointing to her eyes. "How late were you up last night?"

"Umm... three in the morning."

"You really have a death wish. Don't stay up so late tonight."

"I've already finished it," Yan Zhusheng said honestly. "It's only two hundred thousand words. Li Luo, you're so short."

Li Luo: "...Don't just say things that aren't true like that in the future."
